newsitem.title: GERMANY: German agency says rightist violence gains in east.
newsitem.headline: German agency says rightist violence gains in east.

text.p: Neo-nazi violence against foreigners is rising in eastern Germany even though the number of racist attacks nationwide continues to decline, the president of the federal watchdog agency said on Saturday.

Peter Frisch, president of the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), said that there were more attacks in eastern Germany against foreigners and those who look like foreigners so far this year compared to 1996.

"The xenophobic attacks are no longer directed primarily at asylum seekers, but rather against those who do not look or act like 'Germans'," Frisch said in an interview with the Berliner Zeitung newspaper.

"Even if the assailants are not politically motivated, this is still a new form of violence from right-wing extremists," he added. "People are having their basic rights denied because of their origin or their appearance. That is right-wing extremism."
Even though eastern Germany makes up less than one-fifth of Germany's population of 81 million, nearly half of all the racist attacks in 1996 took place in the formerly communist region.
Frisch said the number of racist attacks declined by seven percent nationwide in 1996, but the number rose in the east, where 42 percent of all racist attacks took place.

"So far this year we have seen an upturn in the number of racist attacks in all the eastern German states with the exception of Thuringia," he said. "But it is too early to say if this is the start of a new nationwide trend."
Frisch did not offer an explanation for the upturn in the east, where unemployment is about 20 percent in many areas and nearly double the national average.

Germany was plagued by a sharp rise in right-wing violence after the country's unification in 1990. But the number of violent attacks by right-wing extremists had been falling steadily, from a peak of 2,639 attacks in 1992 to 837 in 1995.
The BfV says there are around 6,000 violent right-wing extremists operating in Germany.
On Friday German police detained 21 people after right-wing extremists went on the rampage across the east in violence that left 14 people injured in several towns.
